new_statements.quote: Stress in Iceve-Maci generally falls on the first stem syllable, but does not have a very prominent realisation. Stress does not play a highly significant role in the phonology. There are nevertheless a few observations that may be related to stress. • Final Vowel Deletion does not apply to the “stressed” syllable (see §7.2, in particular footnote 69). [p. 49] — fn. 69: Stress falls on the stem-initial syllable; Final Vowel Deletion is perhaps limited to unstressed vowels. [p. 38] — §8: Iceve-Maci is a tonal language. It has two contrastive tone levels, High and Low. [p. 41]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Iceve-Maci is a two-level (H/L) tone language. Stress, weakly realised and phonologically marginal, falls on the first syllable of the stem (root), i.e. the syllable after any noun-class prefix — a morphologically anchored stem-initial position rather than word-initial. Evidence offered is indirect: final-vowel deletion spares the stem-initial syllable; the extra CGV contrast and palatalised velars are confined to stem-initial syllables; noun-class suffixes are realised more distinctly after CV than after CVCV roots. If a positional code is wanted the closest is morphological-root (stem-initial).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the author hedges ('generally', 'not a very prominent realisation', 'does not play a highly significant role', observations that 'may be related to stress').
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonological word; stems with class prefixes/suffixes), based on elicited data from the Oliti dialect collected 2008-2013 in Enjawbaw village, Cameroon; Becheve dialect only touched on segmentally. No instrumental data.
new_statements.identity_note: Cox 2013 describes the Oliti dialect of Iceve-Maci (spoken mainly in Cameroon; data from Ogalawen quarter, Enjawbaw village, Manyu Division), with only segmental notes on the Becheve dialect (Nigeria and three villages near Akwaya). Glottolog 5.3 treats Iceve-Maci [icev1238] as a single language; I did not verify whether it assigns dialect-level glottocodes to Oliti or Becheve.
